Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Sub: Annual Report of the Company for the financial year 2025-26 along with the Notice convening the 26th Annual General 
Meeting (‘AGM’) 
In continuation to our letter dated July 24, 2026, intimating the date of 26th AGM of the Company and pursuant to  
Regulations 30 and 34 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing 
Regulations’), please find attached herewith a copy of Annual Report for the financial year 2025-26 along with the Notice of 
the 26th AGM scheduled on Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (IST) through video conferencing.  
Pursuant to Regulation 36 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Annual Report for the financial year 2025-26 along with the 
Notice of the 26th AGM are being dispatched to all the eligible shareholders by electronic means on the e-mail addresses as 
registered with the Company/Registrar and Share Transfer Agent/Depository Participant(s). Further, a physical communication 
is being sent containing the web link and the exact path to access the Annual Report and Notice of the 26th AGM on the 
Company's website to the shareholders whose e-mail addresses are not registered in the records.  
The Annual Report for the financial year 2025-26 and Notice of the 26th AGM have also been made available on the website of 
the Company at www.metropolisindia.com. 
You are requested to take the above information on record. 
Thanking you,  
Yours faithfully, 
 
For Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
 
 
 
Kamlesh C Kulkarni  
Head – Legal & Secretarial

Our Approach to Reporting
At Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
(“Metropolis” or “the Company” or 
"MHL"), we continue to strengthen 
our commitment to high-quality, 
transparent, and stakeholder-centric 
corporate reporting. This Annual 
Report presents an integrated view 
of our performance and progress  
for the financial year ended  
March 31, 2026 (FY 2025-26). It 
offers a comprehensive lens into 
our strategy, business model, 
governance, risks, and outcomes 
across financial and non-financial 
parameters, demonstrating how we 
continue to create sustainable value 
in an evolving healthcare landscape.
Basis of Reporting
For the FY 2025-26 reporting cycle, 
we have further enhanced the depth 
and relevance of our disclosures 
to reflect the needs of a diverse 
stakeholder base, shareholders, 
patients, partners, regulators, 
employees, and the communities 
we serve.
Our reporting approach is guided 
by the principles of connectivity, 
materiality, consistency, 
comparability, and strategic 
orientation, ensuring that 
stakeholders gain meaningful 
insights into our performance and 
future direction.

Corporate Overview

Maximising Capabilities. 
Amplifying Growth.
For over four decades, 
Metropolis Healthcare 
has earned the trust 
of clinicians, hospitals 
and patients through 
scientific excellence, 
diagnostic accuracy and 
uncompromising quality. 
Every investment we 
have made in science, 
technology, digital 
capabilities, laboratory 
infrastructure and 
specialised diagnostics 
has been driven by a 
single belief: stronger 
capabilities create 
stronger outcomes.
FY26 was about unlocking 
the full potential of our 
capabilities – creating 
stronger momentum for 
sustainable growth and 
lasting value.
Building on the strong foundations established 
over the past few years, we shifted our focus 
from expanding capabilities to maximising 
the value they create. Guided by our Maxify 
philosophy of maximising capabilities to amplify 
sustainable growth, we focused on translating 
our investments into stronger execution, higher 
productivity and scalable growth, creating a 
resilient platform for long-term value creation.
At Metropolis, we believe growth is amplified 
when capabilities work together. Scientific 
excellence strengthens clinical confidence. 
Technology enhances productivity. Digital 
innovation improves customer experience. 
Operational discipline reinforces quality and 
consistency. Together, these capabilities create 
a business that is more agile, more resilient and 
better positioned to seize future opportunities 
while delivering value for patients, clinicians, 
partners and shareholders.
FY26 marked an important 
milestone in our journey.

Together, these strategic

Building on the Maxify philosophy, 
FY26 was defined by focused

Capability  
in Action
We embedded quality across every stage of the diagnostic value 
chain through our integrated Quality Intelligence Framework. By 
standardising laboratory practices, strengthening governance 
and leveraging digital quality oversight, we enhanced diagnostic 
accuracy, consistency and compliance, reinforcing trust while 
building a resilient platform for sustainable growth.
Embedding Quality Excellence
We embedded productivity as an organisation-wide discipline 
through workflow optimisation, scientific manpower planning, 
automation and process excellence. By improving resource 
utilisation and operational efficiency, we unlocked greater value 
from our existing network and capabilities.
Driving Enterprise-wide Productivity
We deepened customer engagement by accelerating digital 
adoption, enriching the B2B experience and introducing lifecycle 
management across customer touchpoints. Together, these 
actions delivered more connected, responsive and seamless 
customer journeys.
Advancing Customer-led Growth
We expanded our specialised diagnostics portfolio while 
advancing our genomics capabilities, reinforcing our leadership 
in high-value diagnostics and strengthening our readiness for 
the future of precision medicine.
Strengthening Scientific Leadership
As acquisitions matured, we focussed on integration and value 
realisation. By capturing operational synergies, strengthening 
cross-functional collaboration and institutionalising best 
practices, we enhanced organisational agility and created a 
scalable platform for future growth.
Building an Integrated Enterprise

TruHealth 
Maximising Prevention. 
Amplifying Lifelong Health.
Strengthening Leadership in Preventive Healthcare 
As healthcare increasingly shifts towards prevention and early risk 
identification, TruHealth is strengthening Metropolis' presence in the growing 
preventive healthcare segment through an integrated, patient-centric model. 
By combining advanced diagnostics, comprehensive health assessments and 
expert clinical guidance, TruHealth enables more informed health decisions 
while creating a differentiated preventive healthcare experience. This 
integrated approach continues to drive premiumisation, strengthen customer 
engagement and support long-term growth.

broadening the scope of preventive healthcare and strengthening TruHealth’s differentiated 
market positioning.

is well-positioned to capture the growing demand for preventive healthcare and contribute to 
Metropolis’ long-term sustainable growth.

Specialty Diagnostics
Maximising Precision Diagnostics. 
Amplifying High-Value Growth.
Specialty Diagnostics has become one of Metropolis' key growth drivers, 
powered by a diversified portfolio of advanced diagnostics spanning 
Oncology, Chronic & Infectious Diseases, Gastroenterology, Neurology & 
Nephrology, and Women & Child Health. Combining cutting-edge technologies 
with deep scientific and clinical expertise, we deliver clinically actionable 
insights that strengthen clinician confidence, accelerate premiumisation and 
support sustainable long-term growth.
The integration of CORE Diagnostics has significantly strengthened our precision oncology capabilities, combining 
deep scientific expertise in molecular diagnostics and genomics with Metropolis' nationwide network and trusted 
clinician relationships.

AFRICA & INTERNATIONAL MARKETS:
Over the past decade, Metropolis has established a strong presence in five African countries through company-
managed laboratories and collection centres in Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, Tanzania and Uganda. In addition, we serve 
a diverse network of B2B partners across 16 international markets, including the UAE (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), Oman 
and Qatar in the Middle East; Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Uzbekistan and Vietnam in Asia; and Mauritius, 
Nigeria, Congo, Cameroon, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe in Africa.
Through our international network, we extend access to high-quality diagnostics while leveraging Metropolis’ 
scientific expertise, quality standards and specialised testing capabilities across diverse healthcare markets.

Dear Shareholders,
Every year, I begin this letter by 
asking myself one simple question: 
Did we deliver on the commitments 
we made?
Not only in terms of financial 
performance, but in the way we 
strengthened our science, served 
our patients, supported clinicians, 
empowered our people and 
prepared Metropolis for the future.
Looking back at FY26, I can answer 
that question with confidence. Yes, 
we did.
FY26 was not defined by a single 
milestone. It was the culmination 
of years of deliberate investment 
in scientific capability, technology, 
operational excellence and talent.
Delivering on Our Commitments
The year rewarded that patience. 
Group revenue grew 23.6% to 
` 1,646 crore, EBITDA rose 32% 
to ` 401 crore, and profit after 
tax increased 31% to ` 191 crore. 
Organic revenue growth of 13.7% 
exceeded the guidance of 12–13% 
we had provided at the start of 
the year, while organic margins 
recovered to pre-pandemic levels of 
around 26%. We also kept a promise 
on integration: within four quarters 
of acquisition, Core Diagnostics 
moved from an EBITDA margin of 
negative 2% to high single digits 
— exactly as committed within 
one year.
Beyond the numbers, what 
encourages me most is how we 
grew. Higher patient volumes, 
a richer test mix and better 
productivity drove our growth, 
rather than price increases. To me, 
that is the healthiest kind of growth: 
earned from more patients choosing 
us and more clinicians prescribing 
deeper science, and delivered with 
disciplined capital. The investments 
of the past several years are no 
longer promises on a slide; they are 
showing up in our results.

GLOBAL ECONOMY 
Global economic growth remained stable but moderate, 
with global GDP projected at 3.4% in 2025, moderating to 
3.1% in 2026 before recovering slightly to 3.2% in 2027, 
reflecting a steady but subdued expansion. The global 
outlook continues to be shaped by persistent geopolitical 
tensions, evolving trade dynamics, and uneven regional 
growth patterns.
Ongoing conflicts, including the Russia–Ukraine war 
and instability in the Middle East, remain key sources of 
uncertainty. These developments are exerting pressure 
on energy markets, disrupting supply chains, and 
contributing to volatility in global financial conditions. 
Trade fragmentation and geopolitical disruptions have 
also affected critical commodity flows and key shipping 
routes, resulting in pricing pressures and tighter financial 
conditions, particularly across Asia.
Inflationary pressures are gradually easing, with global 
inflation projected to decline from approximately 4.1% in 
2025 to 3.8% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, although the pace 
of moderation remains uneven across regions. Energy 
price volatility and geopolitical developments continue to 
pose upside risks to inflation, requiring central banks to 
maintain a cautious and balanced policy stance.
Growth trends vary across regions. Advanced economies 
are expected to grow modestly at 1.7%–1.9%, with the 
United States demonstrating relative resilience, while the 
Euro Area and Japan continue to face subdued economic 
momentum. In contrast, Emerging Markets and Developing 
Economies are projected to grow at just above 4%, 
supported by domestic consumption and infrastructure 
investment, although elevated debt levels and tighter 
financial conditions remain key risks.
Regionally, the Middle East continues to demonstrate 
resilience, supported by strong domestic demand, while 
Southeast Asia remains an important growth driver, 
albeit with moderating momentum in certain economies 
following strong performance in the previous year.

and life sciences.

DIAGNOSTICS INDUSTRY
The Indian diagnostics industry continues to be one 
of the fastest-growing segments within the broader 
healthcare ecosystem, supported by increasing health 
awareness, rising disease burden, and improving access 
to diagnostic services. The market was estimated at 
approximately USD 10.9–11.0 billion in 2025, reflecting 
steady expansion driven by rising patient volumes and 
increasing test penetration.
The industry remains highly fragmented, with over 1.3 lakh 
laboratories across the country, dominated by standalone 
laboratories and hospital-based diagnostic centres. 
Standalone laboratories account for approximately 
40–42% of the market, supported by their extensive 
geographic reach and accessibility. However, the industry 
is witnessing a gradual shift towards organised diagnostic 
chains, driven by increasing consumer preference for 
quality, accuracy, and reliability, as well as the need for 
scalable and technology-enabled operations.
This transition towards organised players has accelerated 
in recent years, with the share of organised chains 
increasing from approximately 15% in FY20 to over 22% in 
FY24, supported by consolidation, network expansion, and 
technology adoption. The trend is further reinforced by 
increasing merger and acquisition activity and the growing 
presence of national and regional chains.
From a service mix perspective, pathology continues 
to dominate the diagnostics landscape, accounting for 
approximately 65% of the total market, driven by its routine 
use in disease diagnosis, preventive health check-ups, and 
chronic disease management. Radiology constitutes the 
remaining 35%, including imaging modalities such as X-ray, 
ultrasound, CT scan, MRI, PET-CT, and nuclear imaging.
The industry continues to be largely physician-led, with 
approximately 45–50% of diagnostic volumes originating 
from clinician referrals, reflecting the central role of 
diagnostics in clinical decision-making. At the same time, 
direct-to-consumer engagement is increasing, supported 
by rising health awareness, digital platforms, and the 
growing adoption of preventive healthcare.
Geographically, the diagnostics market remains 
concentrated in urban centres, which account for 
approximately 70–75% of total revenues, supported by 
better healthcare infrastructure, higher awareness, and 
stronger purchasing power. However, this concentration 
also highlights a significant opportunity for expansion 
in Tier II, Tier III, and rural markets. While nearly 70% of 
India’s population resides in rural areas, it contributes only 
~24% of the diagnostics market, indicating substantial

INDUSTRY OUTLOOK
The outlook for the Indian diagnostics industry remains 
strong, supported by favourable demographics, increasing 
health awareness, rising adoption of preventive

ecosystem, are expected to sustain long-term demand

next five years and further expand to approximately USD

by the rising prevalence of non-communicable diseases, 
including diabetes, cardiovascular disorders and cancer, 
increasing health insurance penetration, and growing 
consumer preference for preventive healthcare and early 
disease detection.

shift towards organised diagnostic providers. Expansion

healthcare infrastructure, increasing affordability and

growth opportunities. Organised players are well

trusted brands, quality standards, scalable operating

industry transformation, enhancing diagnostic accuracy, 
operational efficiency and patient experience. Continued 
adoption of automation, digital platforms and advanced

accessibility, reduce turnaround times and support 
scalable growth across the diagnostics value chain.

industry’s long-term fundamentals remain robust. The

technology-enabled diagnostics providers is expected to 
support sustainable growth and long-term value creation.

GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES DRIVING DIAGNOSTICS 
INDUSTRY GROWTH
As diseases increasingly cross borders and health 
awareness grows worldwide, the sector is emerging as a 
critical piece of the country’s healthcare story. The Indian 
diagnostic industry is growing due to regulatory actions by 
the Government of India. A series of policies are launched 
to aid the sector and enhance its accessibility and 
affordability. These shifts are gradually but meaningfully 
reshaping how the diagnostics sector operates - and 
for organised players, which spells a significant long-
term opportunity.
Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya 
Yojana (PM-JAY)
The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana 
(PM-JAY), introduced in 2018, continues to be a cornerstone 
of India’s healthcare reform agenda, providing health 
insurance coverage of up to `5 lakh per family for secondary 
and tertiary care hospitalisation. The scheme has 
significantly expanded access to healthcare services for 
economically vulnerable populations, leading to increased 
healthcare utilisation and earlier disease detection. The 
recent extension of coverage to senior citizens above 
the age of 70 further enhances the inclusivity and reach 
of the programme. The expansion of insurance coverage 
has also contributed to higher diagnostic volumes, as 
hospital-based care pathways increasingly incorporate 
structured testing and screening protocols.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Health and Wellness 
Centres)
The government has made substantial progress in 
strengthening primary healthcare infrastructure through 
the expansion of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, formerly 
known as Health and Wellness Centres. With over 1.78 
lakh centres operational across the country, these 
facilities provide preventive, promotive, and basic 
diagnostic services at the grassroots level. The focus 
on early screening, particularly for non-communicable 
diseases, is enabling timely diagnosis and referral, 
thereby increasing demand for diagnostic services. This 
shift towards preventive care is expected to play a critical 
role in improving long-term health outcomes while driving 
sustained growth in diagnostic testing.
84
Annual Report 2025-26

Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is driving the 
development of a unified digital health ecosystem in 
India. Through the creation of interoperable electronic 
health records and digital health identities, the initiative 
is enabling seamless data exchange across healthcare 
providers. With over 79 crore ABHA IDs generated 
and more than 65 crore health records linked, ABDM is 
improving continuity of care and enabling data-driven 
clinical decision-making. The digital integration of 
healthcare systems is also enhancing diagnostic accuracy, 
streamlining reporting processes, and improving overall 
patient experience.
e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Platform
The government’s e-Sanjeevani platform has emerged 
as a key enabler of telemedicine adoption in India, 
significantly improving healthcare access in remote and 
underserved regions. With over 37 crore consultations 
conducted through a hub-and-spoke model, the platform 
connects primary healthcare centres with specialists 
across the country. This expansion of telemedicine is 
increasingly integrating diagnostics into remote care 
pathways, particularly for follow-up testing, chronic 
disease monitoring, and specialist consultations.
PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission 
(PM-ABHIM)
The PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission 
(PM-ABHIM), with an outlay of approximately `64,000 
crore, aims to strengthen healthcare infrastructure across 
primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The initiative 
focusses on enhancing diagnostic capacity, building 
critical care infrastructure, and improving preparedness for 
future public health emergencies. These investments are 
expected to improve healthcare access and strengthen 
the overall resilience of the healthcare ecosystem.
Free Diagnostics Services Initiative (FDSI)
The Free Diagnostics Services Initiative under the 
National Health Mission is aimed at improving affordability 
and accessibility of diagnostic services by providing 
essential tests at public health facilities. This initiative 
helps reduce out-of-pocket expenditure for patients 
while simultaneously increasing testing volumes 
and strengthening diagnostic infrastructure across 
government healthcare systems.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for 
Medical Devices
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Medical 
Devices is designed to promote domestic manufacturing 
of high-value medical equipment, including diagnostic 
imaging devices such as CT scanners and MRI systems. 
By reducing dependence on imports and encouraging 
local production, the scheme is expected to improve 
accessibility and affordability of advanced diagnostic 
technologies, while strengthening India’s position as a 
manufacturing hub for medical devices.
Biopharma SHAKTI Initiative
The Biopharma SHAKTI initiative represents a significant 
step towards strengthening India’s capabilities in 
pharmaceutical research, biotechnology, and advanced 
diagnostics. With a proposed allocation of approximately 
`10,000 crore, the initiative aims to promote innovation, 
expand clinical trial infrastructure, and support the 
development of next-generation healthcare solutions. 
These efforts are aligned with broader industry trends, 
including increasing investments in high-value diagnostic 
segments such as genomics and oncology.

to proactive prevention, with growing consumer demand 
for genetic testing, early cancer screening, wellness

analytics and longitudinal health data are supporting

skilled professionals, including pathologists, radiologists, 
lab technicians, and phlebotomists. This challenge is more

to talent-related pressures.
Competitive Intensity and Pricing Dynamics
The diagnostics industry continues to witness increasing 
competition from organised chains, hospital-based 
laboratories, and new entrants including digital health 
platforms and pharmaceutical companies. While pricing 
discipline has improved in recent years, competitive

Sustaining competitiveness requires ongoing investment 
in advanced diagnostic technologies, including molecular

costs. The need for specialised personnel to operate such 
technologies further adds to operational expenses, which 
may impact profitability, particularly for smaller and mid-
sized players.
Supply Chain Dependence and Import Exposure
The diagnostics sector remains dependent on imports 
for a significant proportion of reagents, consumables,

Digital Transformation and Data Security Risks
While digitalisation is enhancing efficiency and access, it 
also introduces challenges related to infrastructure gaps 
and data security. The digital divide between urban and 
rural areas may limit the reach of technology-enabled 
services. Additionally, increasing digitisation of patient 
data heightens cybersecurity and data privacy risks, 
necessitating continued investment in secure systems 
and compliance frameworks.
Regulatory Complexity and Compliance Challenges
The regulatory landscape for diagnostics in India 
remains fragmented, with varying levels of adoption 
and enforcement across states. This lack of uniformity 
can increase compliance complexity for multi-location 
operators and may impact standardisation of service 
quality across regions.
Presence of Unorganised and Unregulated 
Laboratories
A significant portion of the diagnostics market continues 
to be served by unorganised players, including laboratories 
operating without standardised accreditation or quality 
controls. This may affect overall service reliability and 
pricing dynamics within the industry, while also posing 
challenges to organised players focussed on maintaining 
high quality and compliance standards.

STRATEGIC ACQUISITIONS AND INTEGRATION
During FY 2025-26, the Company completed three 
strategic acquisitions that strengthened its presence 
in high-growth regional markets. DAPIC Metropolis 
Healthcare Private Limited (formerly known as Metropolis 
Histoxpert Digital Services Private Limited), a wholly-
owned subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare Limited, 
acquired the entire business of Dr. Alok Ahuja and Dr. Alka 
Ahuja and Dr. Ahujas' Pathology & Imaging Centre (DAPIC), 
a partnership firm of Dr. Alok Ahuja and Dr. Alka Ahuja, as 
a going concern, effective May 23, 2025.
Further, Scientific Metropolis Pathology Private Limited 
(formerly known as Metropolis Clinical Pathology Private 
Limited), a subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare Limited, 
acquired the entire business of Dr. Ashok Kumar Sharma's 
Scientific Pathology, a sole proprietorship firm of Dr. Ashok 
Kumar Sharma, as a going concern, effective June 16, 2025.
The Company also acquired the entire business of Dr. RS 
Patil's Ambika Pathology Laboratory, a sole proprietorship 
firm of Dr. Rajendra Sadashiv Patil, comprising pathology 
laboratories in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, as a going concern, 
with effect from September 18, 2025.
From Acquisition to Integration — and Next, Acceleration
FY 2025-26 marked a year in which the Company 
demonstrated its ability to integrate acquired businesses 
effectively. The Company follows a structured integration 
playbook: the first year focusses on integration and 
synergy capture, the second on revenue acceleration, 
and the third on convergence towards company-level 
margins. Guided by a dedicated steering committee, the 
Company integrated four acquisitions – Core Diagnostics, 
Scientific Pathology, DAPIC, and Ambika Pathology-into its 
operating platform by merging overlapping laboratories, 
consolidating procurement, standardising operating 
procedures, and aligning teams around a common 
performance architecture.
The benefits of this disciplined approach are already 
evident. Core Diagnostics exited the year with high single-
digit EBITDA margins and has emerged as a strategic 
platform for the Company's oncology and genomics 
businesses. Scientific Pathology and DAPIC delivered 
growth in line with the Company while operating at margins 
above the Company average. In Kolhapur, the integration 
of Ambika Pathology strengthened the Company's 
regional leadership by creating the largest laboratory in 
the market. Together, the acquired businesses contributed 
approximately 8% of Group revenue and increased North 
India's share of the Company's business from 8% to 17%.
With the first phase of integration complete, FY 2026-27 
will mark the beginning of the second phase-accelerating 
growth by cross-selling specialised test menus across 
acquired channels, deepening clinician engagement, and 
widening access to specialised diagnostics, supported 
by an integration framework that the Company has now 
institutionalised for future opportunities.
RESTRUCTURING
During the year, the Company on February 04, 2026, 
entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to transfer its 
External Quality Assessment Services (EQAS) business to 
its wholly-owned subsidiary, Metropolis Quality Solutions 
Private Limited (MQSPL), on a going concern basis. The 
transfer is intended to enable the EQAS business to 
operate as a separate and independent unit, focussing 
on its core services, with dedicated management and 
resources to drive efficiency, excellence, and growth 
potential. The transfer consideration is up to `1.25 crore, 
subject to closing adjustments, and is proposed to be 
discharged through cash and/or issuance of equity shares 
by MQSPL.

QUALITY AND SCIENTIFIC EXCELLENCE
Quality and scientific excellence remain the cornerstone 
of Metropolis Healthcare Limited's ("the Company") 
competitive differentiation and long-term growth strategy. 
The Company has embedded quality across every stage 
of the diagnostic value chain through its enterprise-
wide Quality Intelligence Framework, which integrates 
governance, digital quality analytics, standardised 
laboratory practices, accreditation, scientific oversight 
and a culture of continuous improvement. This integrated 
framework strengthens diagnostic accuracy, operational 
consistency and regulatory compliance, while reinforcing 
trust among patients, clinicians and institutional partners.
During FY 2025-26, the Company maintained 99.9% 
report accuracy and achieved 100% compliance with 
ISO 15189:2022 across its accredited laboratories, while 
continuing to strengthen quality governance through its 
proprietary Quality Index and technology-enabled quality 
monitoring systems. 
Scientific innovation continued to strengthen the 
Company's leadership in specialised diagnostics. During 
the year, Metropolis strengthened its portfolio by adding 
345 diagnostic tests through new launches and the 
integration of the Core Diagnostics portfolio. These 
included 224 next generation sequencing (NGS) tests and 
50 precision oncology assays, further supporting growth 
in genomics. The Company further strengthened its Centre 
of Genomics through two CAP-accredited laboratories, 
the commissioning of the Illumina’s NovaSeq™ X Series 
and collaborations with leading academic institutions, 
enhancing its capabilities in precision diagnostics and 
advanced molecular testing. During the year, Metropolis 
also became the first listed diagnostics company in India 
to receive a patent in tuberculosis diagnostics, reinforcing 
its commitment to scientific innovation, indigenous 
research and differentiated diagnostic capabilities.
The Company continues to strengthen scientific leadership 
through research, medical education and capability 
development, while investing in the next-generation 
of healthcare professionals through the Metropolis 
Institute of Laboratory Education & Skilling (MiLES). These 
initiatives reinforce the Company's position as a trusted, 
science-led diagnostics organisation and support its long-
term strategy of delivering differentiated, high-quality 
diagnostic services.

organisational agility while supporting business expansion 
and operational excellence.

The Company operates in an intensely 
competitive environment influenced by 
both global and domestic players. Emerging 
competitors and evolving business models 
may increase pricing pressure and influence 
market share. Although the diagnostics 
industry benefits from growing demand and 
long-term expansion potential, heightened 
competition may affect pricing power and 
margins, which could impact profitability 
and returns.
To mitigate the impact of increasing competition, the 
Company continues to strengthen its competitive position 
through scientific differentiation, expansion of specialised 
diagnostics, superior customer experience and sustained 
investments in digital capabilities. It remains focussed on 
cost optimisation, operational excellence and productivity 
enhancement to strengthen margins, improve return ratios and 
drive sustainable growth. 
Simultaneously, the Company continues to expand its 
laboratory network and customer touchpoints, improving 
accessibility, deepening market penetration and supporting 
volume-led growth. The Company’s core business, particularly 
acute illness diagnostics, remains relatively resilient to 
competitive disruption, providing stability in a dynamic 
market environment. In addition, a dedicated Competition 
Desk continuously monitors market dynamics, pricing trends, 
competitive benchmarks and emerging business models, 
enabling timely strategic interventions and reinforcing the 
Company’s competitive positioning.

Innovation Risk
In a rapidly evolving technological 
landscape, the Company faces the risk that 
emerging technologies and continuous 
innovation could render existing systems, 
platforms or services less competitive. 
The increasing adoption of automation, 
artificial intelligence (AI), digital platforms 
and advanced diagnostics is reshaping the 
industry, requiring continuous investments 
in technology upgrades, innovation and 
capability enhancement to maintain 
operational efficiency, service excellence 
and long-term competitiveness.
To address this risk, Metropolis continues to invest in advanced 
technologies, laboratory automation, artificial intelligence 
(AI) and digital platforms to enhance diagnostic accuracy, 
operational efficiency and customer experience. The Company 
is strengthening its technology ecosystem through laboratory 
platform standardisation, intelligent workflow automation, 
AI-enabled diagnostic solutions and enterprise-wide digital 
transformation initiatives. Continuous investments in modern 
laboratory infrastructure, scientific innovation and employee 
capability development ensure the organisation remains agile, 
technologically relevant and well positioned to respond to 
evolving industry requirements.
IT Disruptions and 
System Failure Risk
Given the Company’s extensive reliance 
on technology and data systems, any 
malfunction, cyberattack, or operational 
disruption could negatively impact 
business continuity and service delivery. 
Failure to maintain robust information 
security and governance frameworks may 
expose the Company to risks such as data 
breaches, operational interruptions, and 
reputational damage.
Metropolis has established a robust information security 
and cybersecurity framework, supported by ISO 27001 
and ISO 27701 certifications, reflecting its commitment to 
globally recognised standards for information security and 
privacy management. 
The Company continuously strengthens its cyber resilience 
through secure IT architecture, governance frameworks, 
regular vulnerability assessments, penetration testing and 
independent third-party audits. Continuous monitoring, 
preventive controls and periodic disaster recovery testing 
further enhance business continuity, safeguard patient data 
and ensure uninterrupted operations.
Business Continuity 
Risk
Business operations may be disrupted by 
external events such as natural disasters, 
public health emergencies, civil disturbances, 
geopolitical developments or supply chain 
interruptions. Such events could impact 
laboratory operations, logistics, service 
delivery and the Company's ability to provide 
uninterrupted diagnostic services.
Metropolis has established a comprehensive Business 
Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery (DR) 
framework across its Global Reference Laboratory (GRL) and 
Regional Reference Laboratories (RRLs). Dedicated BCP and 
DR sites, supported by defined response protocols, periodic 
testing and continuous monitoring, help ensure operational 
resilience, minimise service disruptions and maintain 
uninterrupted diagnostic services during unforeseen events.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM
Metropolis Healthcare has instituted a robust internal 
control framework that governs both financial and 
operational functions across the organisation. These 
controls are supported by well-documented policies 
and standard operating procedures designed to ensure 
accurate financial reporting, operational integrity, 
regulatory compliance, and asset protection. 
The internal control system provides reasonable 
assurance regarding the reliability of financial and 
operational information, safeguarding of assets against 
unauthorised use or losses, and adherence to applicable 
laws and regulations. Regular reviews are conducted to 
assess and enhance the effectiveness of these controls. 
The internal audit function, with a clearly-defined 
scope and coverage, plays a critical role in evaluating 
and strengthening the control environment. Key focus 
areas include:
•	
Identifying and reporting key process risks
•	
Verifying compliance with statutory requirements and 
internal guidelines 
•	
Recommending measures to improve process 
efficiency and operational effectiveness
•	
Ensuring the accuracy and dependability of financial 
and operational data.
The Audit Committee of the Board provides active 
oversight, regularly reviewing significant internal audit 
findings and tracking corrective actions. It also monitors 
adherence to accounting standards, evaluates the 
adequacy of risk management practices, and ensures 
that control mechanisms are aligned with the Company’s 
overall governance objectives. This structured and 
proactive approach to internal controls underpins 
Metropolis Healthcare’s commitment to transparency, 
accountability, and sound corporate governance.

These structural trends are expected to create significant 
long-term opportunities for established players with 
strong scientific capabilities, trusted brands and scalable 
operating models.
Building on the strong foundations established over 
the past few years, Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
(“the Company”) is well positioned to capture these 
opportunities through its differentiated scientific 
expertise, technology-enabled operating model, expanding 
network and customer-centric approach. Going forward, 
the Company will remain focussed on driving sustainable

strengthen its market leadership.

framework and a disciplined execution strategy, the

profitable growth and creating long-term value for patients, 
clinicians, shareholders and all other stakeholders.

5.	 Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the 
entity with defined timelines, if any.
Metropolis Healthcare has established a comprehensive set of ESG 
commitments with defined medium- and long-term targets to create 
sustainable value for all stakeholders. 
The Company aims to achieve a 45% reduction in greenhouse gas 
emissions intensity and source ~ 50% of its electricity from renewable 
energy by FY2030, while progressing towards Net Zero emissions 
by FY2043. It is also committed to reducing plastic usage by 50% 
by FY2030, lowering water intensity by 30% by FY2043, and working 
towards Zero Waste to Landfill by FY2030. On the social front, the 
Company aspires to achieve a 50:50 gender-balanced workforce by 
FY2028, maintain a Net Promoter Score (NPS) above 90, and positively 
impact one million lives through its community health initiatives by 
FY2043. 
These commitments are supported by a strong governance framework 
focused on maintaining the highest standards of ethics, regulatory 
compliance, information security, and data privacy. Progress against 
these targets is reviewed periodically through established governance 
mechanisms, ensuring accountability and continuous improvement in 
the Company's ESG performance.
6.	 Performance of the entity against the specific 
commitments, goals and targets along-with 
reasons in case the same are not met.
During FY2025–26, Metropolis Healthcare continued to make 
measurable progress against its ESG commitments across 
environmental stewardship, social responsibility and governance. The 
Company strengthened its environmental performance by sourcing 
approximately 30% of the electricity consumed at the Metropolis 
Global Reference Laboratory from renewable energy, initiating a 100kW 
rooftop solar programme across select facilities, and improving energy 
efficiency through infrastructure upgrades, including LED lighting, HVAC 
optimisation and laboratory process enhancements. Focused initiatives 
in waste management and water conservation further supported 
responsible resource utilisation and operational sustainability.
On the social front, the Company maintained a Net Promoter Score 
(NPS) of 87, reflecting its continued focus on customer satisfaction and 
service excellence. The Company also strengthened its commitment to 
diversity and inclusion, with women constituting ~ 44% of the overall 
workforce. 
From a governance perspective, Metropolis continued to uphold robust 
standards of ethical business conduct, information security and data 
privacy by maintaining ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certifications. Progress 
against ESG commitments is periodically reviewed through established 
governance mechanisms to ensure effective oversight and continuous 
improvement. 
The Company's long-term ESG commitments, including increasing 
renewable energy adoption, reducing emissions intensity, achieving 
Net Zero emissions, improving resource efficiency and strengthening 
workforce diversity, remain on track and are being implemented through 
a phased approach in line with the defined timelines.

At Metropolis Healthcare, sustainability is integral to our purpose of 
enabling healthier lives and creating long-term value for all stakeholders. 
As healthcare continues to evolve, we recognise that delivering 
high-quality diagnostics must go hand in hand with responsible 
environmental stewardship, inclusive growth and strong governance. 
ESG is therefore embedded into our business strategy, guiding decisions 
across our operations, people, innovation and community initiatives.
During FY2025–26, we continued to strengthen our sustainability 
performance through focused investments in energy efficiency, 
renewable energy adoption, responsible waste management and water 
conservation. We also advanced our digital transformation initiatives to 
enhance operational efficiency while reducing resource consumption. 
Across our social agenda, we remained committed to expanding access 
to quality healthcare, strengthening customer trust, fostering an 
inclusive and diverse workplace, and investing in employee capability 
and well-being. Our community programmes continued to create 
measurable social impact by advancing adolescent health, preventive 
healthcare and medical education, in alignment with the United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals.
While we have made meaningful progress, we recognise that the 
transition towards a more sustainable future requires continuous effort 
and collaboration. Increasing climate resilience across our operations, 
accelerating renewable energy adoption, strengthening resource 
efficiency and embedding sustainability across our expanding network 
remain key priorities as we progress towards our long-term ESG 
commitments.
Strong governance remains the cornerstone of our sustainability 
journey. Through robust risk management, ethical business practices, 
information security, regulatory compliance and transparent stakeholder 
engagement, we continue to reinforce trust and accountability across 
our business.
Looking ahead, we remain committed to integrating sustainability into 
every aspect of our organisation. By combining scientific excellence, 
innovation and responsible business practices, we will continue to 
create sustainable value for our patients, employees, partners, investors 
and communities while contributing meaningfully to a healthier and 
more sustainable future.

EI-10. a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the 
entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such system?
Yes. The Company has implemented an Occupational Health and Safety Management System covering its employees, 
operations and facilities. The system is aligned with applicable health, safety and biomedical waste management 
regulations, ISO 15189 requirements, and internal policies. Metropolis continues to monitor occupational health and 
safety performance through established incident reporting, risk assessment and corrective action mechanisms to 
promote a safe and healthy workplace.
EI-10. b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and 
non-routine basis by the entity?
The Company has established processes to identify, assess and manage work-related hazards across its operations. 
Routine risk assessments are carried out through safety inspections, compliance with standard operating procedures 
(SOPs), equipment maintenance, monitoring of personal protective equipment (PPE) usage, and adherence to biosafety 
and biomedical waste management protocols. Non-routine risks are evaluated during the introduction of new equipment, 
process modifications and incident investigations through structured risk assessments, root cause analysis, safety 
audits, mock drills and periodic employee training, enabling timely implementation of preventive and corrective actions. 
EI-10. c. Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove 
themselves from such risks. (Y/N)
Yes. The Company has established processes for employees and workers to report work-related hazards and unsafe 
conditions through their reporting managers, Lab Heads, the Human Resources function or designated safety personnel. 
Employees are encouraged to report concerns promptly and may remove themselves from situations that pose an 
imminent risk to their health or safety until appropriate corrective measures are implemented.
EI-10.d. Do the employees/ worker of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare 
services? (Yes/ No)
All the employees have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services. They are covered either under a 
Group Mediclaim Policy or through ESIC, depending on eligibility and applicability.

EI-1. Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity.
Metropolis Healthcare adopts a structured and ongoing approach to identify and prioritise stakeholders who are impacted 
by, or have the ability to influence, the Company’s business, strategy and sustainability performance. Stakeholder 
groups are identified based on their relationship with the Company, the significance of their influence, the extent of the 
Company’s impact on them, and their relevance to long-term value creation. 
The Company’s key stakeholders include patients, employees, clinicians, investors, suppliers, regulators, business 
partners, communities and other relevant stakeholders. Their perspectives are captured through regular engagement 
mechanisms such as surveys, consultations, feedback platforms, grievance redressal channels, governance forums and 
collaborative partnerships.
Insights from these engagements are integrated into the Company’s risk management, materiality assessment and 
strategic decision-making processes, enabling Metropolis to address stakeholder expectations, strengthen responsible 
business practices and advance its sustainability priorities. The stakeholder identification process is reviewed periodically 
to reflect the evolving business environment, emerging ESG issues and changing stakeholder expectations

LI-1. Provide the processes for consultation between stakeholders and the Board on economic, 
environmental, and social topics or if consultation is delegated, how is feedback from such consultations 
provided to the Board.
Stakeholder engagement on economic, environmental and social matters is primarily undertaken by the respective 
business functions through established engagement channels. Material stakeholder concerns, emerging ESG risks and 
key opportunities are consolidated by the management and reviewed by the Company’s Key Managerial Personnel (KMP). 
Significant matters are periodically presented to the Board of Directors through established governance and reporting 
mechanisms, enabling the Board to provide strategic direction, oversee ESG priorities and incorporate stakeholder 
perspectives into business decisions and long-term strategy.

LI-2. Whether stakeholder consultation is used to support the identification and management of 
environmental, and social topics (Yes / No). If so, provide details of instances as to how the inputs received 
from stakeholders on these topics were incorporated into policies and activities of the entity.
Yes. Stakeholder consultations form an integral part of the Company’s approach to identifying and managing 
environmental and social priorities. During the year, Metropolis undertook a materiality assessment using a double 
materiality approach, engaging key stakeholder groups to understand their expectations and assess the impact of ESG 
issues on the business and society. The insights were used to prioritise material ESG topics, strengthen the Company’s 
sustainability roadmap, and inform policies, targets and initiatives relating to climate action, responsible operations, 
employee well-being, customer experience and community impact.
LI-3. Provide details of instances of engagement with, and actions taken to, address the concerns of 
vulnerable/ marginalized stakeholder groups.
Metropolis Healthcare engages with vulnerable and marginalised communities through its CSR and public health 
programmes, with a focus on improving access to healthcare, health awareness and medical education. Through initiatives 
such as the Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health (ARSH) programme, preventive healthcare initiatives and 
MedEngage, the Company regularly engages adolescents, underserved communities and economically disadvantaged 
medical students to understand their needs and barriers to access.
Insights from these engagements have informed programme enhancements, including strengthening referral linkages 
with public health systems, expanding peer educator and community health worker models, adopting behaviour change 
communication approaches, and improving programme accessibility and outreach. These actions have strengthened 
programme effectiveness while enabling the Company to create sustainable social impact in underserved communities.

details.
Yes. The Company has implemented initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across its operations. 
Renewable energy is sourced through third-party Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for solar power at select locations. 
At the Global Reference Laboratory (GCA), one of the Company's largest facilities, approximately 30% of electricity 
requirements are currently met from renewable sources.
The Company has also progressively replaced conventional air conditioning units with energy-efficient systems using 
R32 refrigerant, which has a lower Global Warming Potential (GWP) than the refrigerants previously in use.
Together, these measures have reduced the Company's dependence on grid electricity and lowered Scope 1 and Scope 
2 emissions.

Brief outline on CSR & ESG Policy of the Company:
	
At Metropolis Healthcare Limited (“the Company” or “Metropolis”), contributing to society is a fundamental value. 
For over four decades, we have remained dedicated to enhancing the quality of life in the communities we serve. 
Our approach to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is deeply aligned with our vision and mission, emphasizing 
not only business growth but also positive social impact.
	
Our flagship CSR initiatives are closely aligned with key United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(SDGs), including:
	
•	
Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3)
	
•	
Quality Education (SDG 4)
	
•	
Gender Equality (SDG 5)
	
These focus areas shape the foundation of all our CSR efforts.
	
The Company’s CSR & ESG Policy (“the Policy”), as approved by the Board of Directors, is available on the official 
Metropolis website. Our CSR initiatives are designed to align with and support the objectives outlined in this Policy.
	
Key CSR Initiatives
	
A key initiative under our CSR framework is the foundation established by the CSR & ESG Committee, which focuses 
on empowering adolescent girls by providing accurate information on reproductive health and essential life skills. 
This initiative seeks to educate and enable adolescents to make informed decisions and lead empowered lives.
	
Through our preventive healthcare programs, we engage directly with communities to raise awareness about health 
and wellness, promoting the importance of preventive care for building a healthier society.
	
Our flagship program, MedEngage, supports aspiring medical professionals by offering scholarships and research 
grants, nurturing the next generation of healthcare leaders.
	
Metropolis consistently implements community-focused initiatives that deliver tangible and lasting impact, 
particularly in areas surrounding our operations. Our efforts prioritize underprivileged and marginalized communities, 
aiming to uplift and empower them. We remain committed to creating long-term stakeholder value by being socially 
responsible, inclusive, and focused on improving health, education, and overall well-being for all.

growth but also towards maximization of benefits for its shareholders, employees, customers and the general

which ensures that the organization is managed and monitored in a responsible manner for creating and sharing 
stakeholders value. 
	
Your Company is committed to good corporate governance and adherence to best practices. Its philosophy is 
based on five basic elements namely, accountability, value creation, strategic-guidance, transparency and equitable

BOARD OF DIRECTORS 
	
Composition of Board
	
The Board comprises an appropriate combination of Executive, Non-Executive and Independent Directors including 
one Woman Independent Director in compliance with the requirements of Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”), SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) and the Articles 
of Association of the Company. 
	
This composition reflects an optimal blend of professionalism, knowledge, expertise and experience which enables 
the Board to discharge its responsibilities effectively and provide sound leadership to the Company’s business. 
	
As on March 31, 2026, the Board Composition of the Company was as follows: 10 (ten) Directors of which 5 (five) 
are Non-Executive Independent Directors, 3 (three) are Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors and 2 (two) are 
Executive Directors. Brief profile of the Directors is available on the website of the Company at click here and forms 
part of this Annual Report. 
	
Board and Committee Meetings 
	
The Board and Committee Meetings are pre-scheduled and the annual calendar is shared with Directors in advance 
to ensure their availability. The Board meets at least once every quarter to review and discuss the Company’s 
performance, quarterly financial results, and other important matters. The agenda along with explanatory notes 
thereto of the business(es) to be transacted at the Board and Committee Meetings are circulated well in advance 
to the Board/ respective Committees of the Company in compliance with the requirements of the Act. 
	
Further, video-conferencing facilities are also provided to facilitate Directors travelling/ residing abroad or at other 
locations to participate in the meetings. The necessary quorum was present for all the meetings. The Management 
team provides update on key areas such as business performance, functional outcomes etc. In case of urgent 
matters, approvals are sought by way of circular resolution.

the Company in identification, assessment, prioritization and to mitigate, monitor and report the risks. 
	
During the year under review, 2 (two) meetings of Risk Management Committee were held on May 12, 2025 and 
November 20, 2025. The Board has accepted all recommendations made by the Risk Management Committee during 
the year.
	
The Chairperson of the Risk Management Committee attended the 25th AGM held on August 13, 2025. 
	
The brief terms of reference of the Risk Management Committee, inter alia, include the following:
	
1.	
Oversee and guide in developing a structured/ defined framework for identifying and assessing and reporting of 
both existing and new risks associated with the Company so as to facilitate timely and effective management 
of risks and opportunities for achieving the Company’s objectives;
	
2.	
Periodic review of Risk Management Framework ("the framework") comprising of policies, procedures and 
practices of the Company and to assess the effectiveness of the same and initiate corrective actions wherever 
required including any change that may be required to the framework in the light of various external and 
internal factors (whether political, sociological or technical or other) which will have impact on the business of 
the company;
	
3.	
Adopt and review periodically best business practices and policies;
	
4.	
Review and monitor compliance with the regulatory framework and the statutory requirements;
	
5.	
Set/ define standardised approach for minimization and mitigation of identified risks;
	
6.	
Review and guide the senior management from time to time in setting up a work culture which would encourage 
staff/ team of the Company at all levels to identify risks and opportunities and respond them effectively;
	
7.	
Review reports on any material breaches of risk limits/ parameters and the adequacy of the proposed 
action; and

POLICIES AND PROCESSES
Code of Conduct for Board Members and Senior Management Personnel (‘Code’)
	
The Company’s Code is the principal document which stems on the core values of the Company viz (i) Commitment to 
excellence; (ii) Integrity including intellectual honesty, openness, fairness and trust; (iii) Care for people; (iv) Socially-
valued enterprise and  (v) Business Integrity with focus to become a dynamic and successful business organization. 
	
All the Directors and Senior management are mandated to conduct themselves honestly, fairly, ethically and 
with integrity, and to maintain the highest standards of professional, courteous and respectful behaviour in their 
interactions. They are required to submit an annual affirmation confirming compliance with the Code.
	
All Board members and Senior Management Personnel have affirmed their compliance with the Code for the 
financial year 2025-26. A declaration on compliance with the Code, duly signed by Mr. Surendran Chemmenkotil, 
Managing Director of the Company, forms part of this Report.
	
Conflict of Interest
	
The Company has established a process to proactively identify and avoid conflicts of interest. As a part of this 
process, each Director is required to disclose, on an annual basis or upon any change during the year, their interests 
in other entities, including Board and Committee Memberships/ Chairpersonships held in other companies. The 
Board members exercise due care and avoid any conflict of interest while discharging their duties, particularly

in the decision-making process. The members of the Board restrict themselves from any decision and voting in 
transaction that they have concern or interest.  
Policy on Related Party Transactions ("RPT Policy")
	
All transactions entered into with the Related Parties during financial year 2025-26 were in the ordinary course 
of business, on an arm’s length basis and in compliance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made 
thereunder, the SEBI Listing Regulations, and the Company’s RPT Policy. No materially significant Related Party 
Transactions were entered into during the financial year that would attract the provisions of Regulation 23 of the 
SEBI Listing Regulations. 
	
As a process all the Related Party Transactions are placed before the Audit Committee for its approval and a 
statement of Related Party Transaction is also placed before the Audit Committee on quarterly basis to ensure 
the transactions remain within the limits approved by the Audit Committee.
	
During the financial year, the Audit Committee, at its meeting held on August 07, 2025, recommended amendments in 
the RPT Policy to the Board to align it with the regulatory changes introduced by the SEBI, which were subsequently 
reviewed and approved by the Board, to ensure continued compliance with the revised regulatory framework.
	
Details of all Related Party Transactions entered during the financial year 2025-26 are set out in note no. 38 of the 
Standalone Financial Statements.
	
Policy on Materiality
	
The Company has adopted a Policy for determining Materiality of Events & Information in line with the requirements 
of Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations.
	
This policy outlines the criteria for determining any material event/ information which may require disclosure to 
the Stock Exchanges. An event/information is treated as material based on the materiality threshold viz. deemed 
material, quantitative and qualitative criteria for triggering of events. 
	
The Company conducts awareness programs for key stakeholders to ensure familiarity with the processes for 
identifying, handling and disclosing material events and information. The contact details of Key Managerial Personnel 
authorized to determine and disclose the material information/ event are available on the website of the Company 
at click here.
	
Policy for determining "Material Subsidiaries"
	
As on March 31, 2026, the Company does not have any material unlisted subsidiary as defined under Regulation 16 
and 24 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. However, as a process, and to ensure identification of material subsidiary 
in near future, the Company has formulated a policy for determining material subsidiaries in terms of the SEBI 
Listing Regulations. 
	
The Board of the Company, or its duly constituted Committees, exercises oversight over the affairs of its subsidiaries 
and regularly reviews key information pertaining to them, including:
	
•	
Minutes of the Board meetings; 
	
•	
Summary of Financial performance; 
	
•	
Material borrowing by subsidiaries and guarantees given, if any; 
	
•	
Related party transactions entered into by the subsidiaries; 
	
•	
Utilisation of funds and details of investment and advances;
	
•	
Material developments, financial & operating performance; and
	
•	
Review of significant transactions or arrangements entered into by the unlisted subsidiaries.
	
Policy on Dividend Distribution
	
The Company has adopted Dividend Distribution Policy in accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, setting out the parameters and circumstances that shall be considered by the Board in determining 
the declaration of dividends to the shareholders.

Policy on Preservation and Archival of documents & records
	
The Company has adopted a policy on Preservation and Archival of documents & records for preservation of 
documents in terms of Regulation 9 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The Policy provides a framework for the 
maintenance, preservation, archival, and disposal of the Company’s documents and records.
Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading
	
In compliance with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI PIT Regulations”) as amended from 
time to time, the Company has formulated a comprehensive Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading 
(“PIT Code”) to regulate and monitor trading by Designated Persons and their immediate relatives, in securities of 
the Company. 
	
The Code outlines procedures to be followed by designated persons while trading in Company’s shares, and while 
handling or sharing Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”). It sets out the Company’s obligations to:
	
a.	
maintain a structured digital database;
	
b.	
implement mechanisms for prevention of insider trading and ensure proper handling of UPSI;
	
c.	
raise awareness about the sensitivity of UPSI.
	
During the financial year the Company conducted various awareness programs highlighting Dos and Don’ts, the 
penal consequences of non-adherence to the Code and the necessity to maintain Structured Digital Database. 
The Company has also adopted Code of Fair Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information & Policy for 
Legitimate Purpose. 
	
The Compliance Officer is responsible for monitoring adherence of the PIT Code and SEBI PIT Regulations.
	
Code of Business Conduct & Ethics
	
The Company has in place a Code of Business Conduct & Ethics, (“Code of Conduct”), which is a cornerstone of 
its purpose and values and reflects its commitment to the highest standards of ethics, integrity and responsible 
business practices. The Code guides all Associates in conducting business in compliance with applicable laws, 
regulations and accepted national and international standards. The Company maintains a zero-tolerance approach 
towards any breach of the Code or applicable laws, and no commercial or financial consideration shall be deemed 
sufficient to justify non-compliance.
	
During the financial year under review, 32 complaints were received under the Code of Conduct, including 10 
complaints carried forward from FY 2024-25, a total of 42 complaints were dealt with during FY 2025-26, of which 
33 were resolved and 9 remained pending as at the end of the financial year.
	
Vigil mechanism
	
The Company has in place a Whistle Blower Policy incorporating vigil mechanism in accordance with Regulation 22 
of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The Policy provides an avenue for employees to raise concerns that could have a 
significant impact on the operations, performance, value, and reputation of the Company, and empowers the Audit 
Committee to investigate such concerns.
	
The Policy also provides for a dedicated email ID viz compliance@metropolisindia.com and in exceptional cases, 
the whistle blower can also approach the Audit Committee Chairman at audit.chairman@metropolisindia.com.for 
reporting genuine concerns including concerns on anonymous basis without fear of being reprimanded. No person 
was denied access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee.
	
During the financial year, no complaints were received under the Company's Whistle Blower Policy.

Impairment assessment of Goodwill and Intangible asset with indefinite life
See Note 4 to standalone financial statements
The key audit matter
How the matter was addressed in our audit
As disclosed in Note 4, the Company’s standalone financial 
statements includes Goodwill aggregating Rs 41,542.55 lakhs 
pertaining to past acquisitions/ amalgamations. Further, the 
Company’s standalone financial statements also includes 
intangible assets with indefinite life (‘Brand’) aggregating Rs 
30,221.25 lakhs, which was acquired pursuant to business 
acquisitions, which together represent 38% of total assets of the 
Company as at 31 March 2026.
The Company tests goodwill and indefinite life intangible asset 
for impairment annually, or more frequently when there is an 
indication that the cash generating unit (‘CGU’) to which goodwill 
and the indefinite life intangible asset has been allocated may 
be impaired.
The recoverable value of the CGU has been derived using 
discounted cash flow model.
Our audit procedures included:
	•
Understanding the process followed by the Company in 
respect of the annual impairment analysis and assess the 
appropriateness of accounting policy.
	•
Evaluating the design and implementation and testing the 
operating effectiveness of key internal financial controls 
related to the Company’s process of performing impairment 
assessment, including controls over determination of key 
assumptions used in such assessment.
	•
Evaluating the reasonableness of the key assumptions, used 
in the cash flow forecasts which includes projected earnings 
before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), 
revenue growth rates and cost assumptions.
	•
Assessing the historical accuracy of management’s forecasts 
by comparing past forecasts to actual results achieved.
	•
Involving valuation professionals with specialised skills and 
knowledge, where necessary, to assist in evaluating the 
impairment model used and assumptions including discount 
rate and terminal growth rate applied by the Company, by 
comparing it to a range of rates that were independently 
developed using publicly available market indices and market 
data for comparable entities.

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the 
Company’s internal financial controls with reference to 
financial statements based on our audit. We conducted 
our audit in accordance with the Guidance Note and 
the Standards on Auditing, prescribed under Section 
143(10) of the Act, to the extent applicable to an audit 
of internal financial controls with reference to financial 
statements. Those Standards and the Guidance Note 
require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan 
and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance 
about whether adequate internal financial controls with 
reference to financial statements were established and 
maintained and if such controls operated effectively in all 
material respects.
Our audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit 
evidence about the adequacy of the internal financial 
controls with reference to financial statements and their 
operating effectiveness. Our audit of internal financial 
controls with reference to financial statements included 
obtaining an understanding of internal financial controls 
with reference to financial statements, assessing the 
risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and 
evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of 
internal control based on the assessed risk. The procedures 
selected depend on the auditor’s judgement, including the 
assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the 
standalone financial statements, whether due to fraud or 
error. 
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is 
sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit 
opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls with 
reference to financial statements.
Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with 
Reference to Financial Statements
A company's internal financial controls with reference to 
financial statements is a process designed to provide 
reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial 
reporting and the preparation of financial statements 
for external purposes in accordance with generally 
accepted accounting principles. A company's internal 
financial controls with reference to financial statements 
include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain 
to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable 
detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and 
dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide 
reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as 
necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in 
accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, 
and that receipts and expenditures of the company are 
being made only in accordance with authorisations of 
management and directors of the company; and (3) provide 
reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely 
detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition 
of the company's assets that could have a material effect 
on the financial statements.

Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, including the 
possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud 
may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference 
to financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial controls with reference to 
financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with 
the policies or procedures may deteriorate.

Background of the Company and nature of 
operations
Metropolis Healthcare Limited (the 'Company'), was 
incorporated in India as Pathnet India Private Limited 
in the year 2000 and is engaged in the business of 
providing pathology and related healthcare services. 
The registered office of the Company is located at 
4th Floor, East Wing,Plot-254 B, Nirlon House, Dr.Annie 
Besant Road, Worli. Mumbai - 400030. The Company 
got listed on Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and 
National Stock Exchange (NSE) on 15 April 2019 
through sale of equity shares by Dr. Sushil Shah and 
CA Lotus Investments.

material accounting policies
2.1	 Basis of preparation and measurement
a	
Statement of compliance:
The Standalone Balance Sheet of the Company 
as at 31 March 2026 and the Standalone 
Statement of Profit and Loss (including Other 
Comprehensive Income), the Standalone 
Statement of Changes in Equity and the 
Standalone Statement of Cash flows for the 
year ended 31 March 2026 and summary of 
material accounting policies and other financial 
information (together referred as ‘Standalone 
Financial Statements’) has been prepared under 
Indian Accounting Standards ('Ind AS') notified 
under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 
read with the Companies (Indian Accounting 
Standards) Rules, 2015, as amended from time 
to time.
The Standalone Financial Statements of the 
Company for year ended 31 March 2026 were 
authorised for issue in accordance with a 
resolution of the Board of Directors on 13 
May 2026.
The accounting policies are applied consistently 
to all the periods presented in the Standalone 
Financial Statements, unless stated otherwise.
These financial Statements are presented in 
Indian rupees, which is also the company's 
functional currency. All amounts have 
been rounded to the nearest lakhs unless 
otherwise indicated.
b	
Current vs non-current classification:
All the assets and liabilities have been classified 
into current and non current.
Assets:
An asset is classified as current when it satisfies 
any of the following criteria:
a)	
it is expected to be realised in, or is intended 
for sale or consumption in, the Company’s 
normal operating cycle;
b) 	
it is held primarily for the purpose of 
being traded;
c)	
it is expected to be realised within twelve 
months after the reporting date; or
d)	
it is cash or cash equivalent unless it is 
restricted from being exchanged or used to 
settle a liability for at least twelve months 
after the reporting date.
Liabilities:
A liability is classified as current when it satisfies 
any of the following criteria:
a)	
it is expected to be settled in the Company’s 
normal operating cycle;
b)	
it is held primarily for the purpose of 
being traded;
c)	
it is due to be settled within twelve months 
after the reporting date; or
d)	
the 
Company 
does 
not 
have 
an 
unconditional right to defer settlement of 
the liability for at least twelve months after 
the reporting date. 
Terms of a liability that could, at the option of 
the counterparty, result in its settlement by 
the issue of equity instruments do not affect 
its classification.
Operating cycle:
All assets and liabilities have been classified 
as current or non-current as per the Company's 
normal operating cycle and other criteria set 
out in Schedule III to the Companies Act 2013. 
Based on the nature of services and the time 
taken between acquisition of assets/inventories 
for processing and their realization in cash and 
cash equivalents, the Company has ascertained 
its operating cycle as twelve months for the 
purpose of the classification of assets and 
liabilities into current and non-current.

Measurement of fair values
Company’s accounting policies and disclosures 
require the measurement of fair values, for both 
financial and non-financial assets and liabilities.
Fair value is the price that would be received 
to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability 
in an orderly transaction between market 
participants at the measurement date. A fair 
value measurement of a non-financial asset 
takes into account a market participant’s ability 
to generate economic benefits by using the 
asset in its highest and best use or by selling it 
to another market participant that would use the 
asset in its highest and best use.

Fair values are categorized into different levels 
in a fair value hierarchy based on the inputs used 
in the valuation techniques as follows. 
Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) in active 
markets for identical assets or liabilities.
Level 2: inputs other than quoted prices included 
in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or 
liability, either directly (i.e. as prices) or indirectly 
(i.e. derived from prices).
Level 3: inputs for the asset or liability that 
are not based on observable market data 
(unobservable inputs).
If the inputs used to measure the fair value of 
an asset or a liability fall into different levels 
of the fair value hierarchy, then the fair value 
measurement is categorized in its entirety in 
the same level of the fair value hierarchy as 
the lowest level input that is significant to the 
entire measurement.
The Company recognises transfers between 
levels of the fair value hierarchy at the end of 
the reporting year during which the change 
has occurred.

2.2	 Material accounting policies
a)	 Business combinations
Common Control:
Business combinations arising from transfers of 
interests in entities that are under the control of 
the shareholders that control the Company are 
accounted for as if the acquisition had occurred 
at the beginning of the earliest comparative 
period presented or, if later, at the date that 
common control was established; for this 
purpose comparatives are revised.
Business combinations involving entities that 
are ultimately controlled by the same parties 
before and after the business combination are 
considered as Common control entities and are 
accounted using the pooling of interest method 
as follows:
	
– The assets and liabilities of the combining 
entities are reflected at their carrying 
amounts.
	
– No adjustments are made to reflect the fair 
values, or recognise new assets or liabilities. 
Adjustments are made to harmonise 
accounting policies.
	
– The financial information in the financial 
statements in respect of prior periods is 
restated as if the business combination 
has occurred from the beginning of the 
preceding period in the financial statements, 
irrespective of the actual date of the 
combination.
	
– The balance of the retained earnings 
appearing in the financial statements 
of the transferor is aggregated with the 
corresponding balance appearing in the 
financial statements of the transferee or is 
adjusted against general reserve.
	
– The identity of the reserves are preserved 
and the reserves of the transferor become 
the reserves of the transferee.
	
– The difference if any, between the amounts 
recorded as share capital plus any additional 
consideration in the form of cash or other 
assets and the amount of share capital 
of the transferor is transferred to capital 
reserve and is presented separately from 
other capital reserves.
Other than common control business 
combinations:
The Company applies the acquisition method 
to account for business combination. The 
consideration transferred for the acquisition of 
a business comprises the:
	
– fair values of the assets transferred,
	
– liabilities incurred to the former owners of 
the acquired business,
